title: Psychologically Informed Physical Therapy Management of Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain in Culturally Diverse Populations: An Intervention Logic Model
authors: Katrina S. Monroe; Kristin R. Archer; Stephen T. Wegener; Sara P. Gombatto
pain_condition_detail: chronic musculoskeletal pain, chronic spine pain, low back pain, neck pain
context_note: Focus on culturally and linguistically diverse (CALD) populations, specifically US Latino persons near US-Mexico border.
bps_function_set: background framing; critique or problematization; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses BPS as a foundation for PIPT but focuses on bio (exercise, physical activity) and psycho (cognitive skill training) domains, explicitly noting that social factors are rarely addressed. It proposes a logic model integrating these domains for culturally diverse populations, but does not define the BPS model itself.
integration_mechanism_summary: The model proposes that PIPT interventions (cognitive skill training + exercise) reduce pain-related disability through psychological mediators (psychological flexibility, self-efficacy, reduced catastrophizing/fear avoidance) and physical mediators (improved movement patterns). Social factors are contextual moderators but not integrated into the causal pathway.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper uses BPS as a foundation but explicitly notes that social factors are rarely addressed in BPS-labeled PT, creating a tension between the model's claim and its operationalization
conceptual_tensions_2: The logic model integrates bio and psych domains via mediators but treats social factors as contextual moderators rather than integrated components, reflecting a partial triadic integration
conceptual_tensions_3: Psychological constructs like catastrophizing and fear avoidance are named but not formally defined, relying on assumed shared meaning
additional_observations_1: The paper proposes a logic model for PIPT that is explicitly designed to be culturally tailored, but the general model itself does not include social factors as essential intervention components
additional_observations_2: The paper's literature review on Latino populations provides rich social and cultural detail, but this is not integrated into the causal pathway of the logic model
additional_observations_3: The paper critiques existing BPS frameworks for lacking specificity and sociocultural consideration, yet its own model does not fully operationalize the social domain
synthesis_note: This paper uses BPS as a foundation for PIPT but operationalizes it primarily as bio+psych, with social factors acknowledged but not integrated into the causal model. It explicitly critiques BPS-labeled PT for neglecting social factors, yet its own logic model does not fully address this gap. The paper is valuable for its focus on cultural tailoring and its explicit identification of conceptual problems with BPS.
coding_rationale: Typology is pseudo_bps because BPS language is used but social domain is thin and not integrated. Triadic integration is partial: bio and psych are linked via mediators, social is contextual. Psych-dominant due to elaborated psychological constructs.

citation: Monroe et al. (2025), The journal of pain
title: Psychologically Informed Physical Therapy Management of Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain in Culturally Diverse Populations: An Intervention Logic Model
authors: Katrina S. Monroe; Kristin R. Archer; Stephen T. Wegener; Sara P. Gombatto
pain_condition_detail: Chronic musculoskeletal pain; examples include low back pain, neck pain, and chronic spine pain.
context_note: Illustration focuses on US Hispanic/Latino persons seeking care for chronic spine pain at a Federally Qualified Health Center near the United States-Mexico border; broader context includes CALD populations and low- and middle-income nations.
bps_function_set: background framing; critique or problematization; intervention rationale; justification; operational definition; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper turns the BPS frame into a PIPT logic model: cognitive skill training plus aerobic activity, therapeutic exercise, and graded functional movement. It specifies determinants such as psychological flexibility, self-efficacy, catastrophizing, fear, and pain beliefs, and tailors them to sociocultural factors such as language, health literacy, familismo, personalismo, and social support.
integration_mechanism_summary: PIPT combines cognitive skill training with aerobic activity, therapeutic exercise, and graded functional movement. The proposed pathway is active cognitive and physical coping behaviors, mediated by psychological flexibility, self-efficacy, reduced catastrophizing/fear/maladaptive beliefs, leading to less pain/disability and greater work/social participation. Sociocultural factors are proposed as moderators/mediators and tailoring guides, not a fully specified three-domain mechanism.
emergent_labels_12: Medical Outcomes Study Social Support Measure
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper critiques existing biopsychosocial/PIPT frameworks for missing socioeconomic, ethnocultural, and interpersonal factors while proposing a PIPT model that remains centered on physical therapy interventions
conceptual_tensions_2: The general model is grounded in PIPT evidence, yet the authors state that mediators may differ in CALD populations and must be tested
conceptual_tensions_3: Social factors are central to tailoring and proposed as mediators/moderators, but the core mechanism remains primarily cognitive-emotional and physical
conceptual_tensions_4: The paper calls for culturally relevant care while acknowledging that existing rehabilitation frameworks are vague, difficult to test, and limited to behavioral mechanisms
conceptual_tensions_5: Prayer and remedios are incorporated as culturally relevant coping options alongside evidence-based PIPT techniques
additional_observations_1: This is a perspective/intervention logic model, not an empirical test of the proposed mechanisms
additional_observations_2: The Latino example is operationalized in a Federally Qualified Health Center near the United States-Mexico border
additional_observations_3: The social domain is more developed than in many PIPT papers but functions mainly as tailoring, moderator, mediator, and contextual determinant
additional_observations_4: The paper does not provide formal definitions for most psychological constructs beyond psychological flexibility
additional_observations_5: The article reports no quality-of-evidence appraisal because of its scoping/narrative nature
additional_observations_6: No spiritual/religious framework is developed, prayer is treated as a coping option rather than a formal construct
synthesis_note: The paper operationalizes BPS as a PIPT logic model: physical therapy components plus cognitive-emotional skill training plus sociocultural tailoring. It goes beyond listing domains by specifying mediators/moderators and culturally relevant constructs, but the social domain mainly functions as context/tailoring for a biopsychosocial PIPT mechanism rather than as an independently modeled causal system.
coding_rationale: All three domains are present and linked, but the social domain is mostly a moderator/tailoring layer; therefore triadic integration is partial rather than a fully specified three-way mechanism.

title: Psychologically Informed Physical Therapy Management of Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain in Culturally Diverse Populations: An Intervention Logic Model
authors: Katrina S. Monroe; Kristin R. Archer; Stephen T. Wegener; Sara P. Gombatto
pain_condition_detail: chronic musculoskeletal pain in culturally and linguistically diverse populations
context_note: US-Mexico border health center serving Latino population
bps_function_set: background framing; critique or problematization; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: Uses BPS as organizing framework for PIPT interventions but critiques its failure to address social factors. Develops intervention logic model with essential elements for cultural adaptation.
conceptual_tensions_1: BPS label is used but social domain is critiqued as absent from PIPT practice
conceptual_tensions_2: Psychological constructs are well-developed but lack integration with biological and social domains
conceptual_tensions_3: Cultural adaptation is proposed but mechanisms of cultural influence are not specified
conceptual_tensions_4: Intervention logic model is presented but lacks empirical testing of proposed pathways
additional_observations_1: The paper uses BPS terminology extensively but does not define the model itself, only citing Engel's model as foundation
additional_observations_2: Essential interventions are identified as cognitive skill training, aerobic activity, therapeutic exercise, and functional movement training
additional_observations_3: Cultural adaptation for Latino population includes addressing fatalismo, familismo, and personalismo
additional_observations_4: The logic model proposes psychological flexibility and self-efficacy as key mediators but does not specify biological or social pathways
synthesis_note: This paper uses the biopsychosocial model as an organizing framework for PIPT interventions but critically notes that social factors are rarely addressed in practice. It develops an intervention logic model with four essential elements (cognitive skill training, aerobic activity, therapeutic exercise, functional movement training) and identifies psychological constructs like catastrophizing, fear avoidance, and self-efficacy as key mediators. The paper emphasizes cultural adaptation for Latino populations, incorporating constructs like fatalismo and familismo. However, the BPS integration is superficial - biological and social domains are mentioned but not meaningfully integrated with psychological
coding_rationale: BPS typology is multifactorial because all three domains are present but not integrated. Psychological domain is elaborated with multiple constructs, biological and social are mentioned but not developed. Integration is 'none' because domains are treated in parallel without specified pathways between them.
